paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The chart titled “QAdapter” illustrates GPU memory usage for several fine-tuning approaches, with one bar per method. The categorical axis is horizontal and lists the methods (shown as diagonally rotated labels) in the displayed order: Full FT, MTL-FT, TAG, Adapter, QAdapter, and Ours; there is no secondary grouping or stacking. The value axis is vertical, labeled “GPU Memory (GB),” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0, 20, 40, and 60 GB, spanning from 0 up to a little above 70 GB. The bars are solid-filled, with the first five methods shown in orange and the final method (“Ours”) shown in green; approximate bar heights are Full FT at about 73 GB, MTL-FT at about 43 GB, TAG at about 19 GB, Adapter at about 16–17 GB, QAdapter at about 8–9 GB, and Ours at about 19 GB. The methods do not appear to be sorted by height, and the “Ours” category is visually emphasized by using a different bar color (green) and a heavier/bolder x-axis label compared with the others.
